summary.title: GrandCode: Achieving Grandmaster Level in Competitive Programming via Agentic Reinforcement Learning

details: Competitive programming under live-contest conditions remains a domain where the best AI systems still trail top humans (prior best: Gemini 3 Deep Think, 8th place on historical problems).

GrandCode: a multi-agent RL system that orchestrates a main solver policy plus auxiliary hypothesis-generation, long-trace summarization, and adversarial test-case generation modules, jointly optimized by post-training RL and per-problem online test-time RL.

Agentic GRPO: a GRPO variant for multi-stage agentic rollouts that updates the policy immediately on each stage's intermediate reward r_t and later applies a separately group-normalized 'delayed correction' advantage on (r_N - r_t) once the final reward arrives, mitigating delayed-reward and off-policy drift.
Main solver: Qwen 3.5-397B MoE (hybrid 3 DeltaNet + 1 softmax attention per block), multimodal input used natively for figure-containing problems.
Auxiliary policies pi_hypothesis and pi_summary: Qwen-3.5-27B dense models, SFT then GRPO, served on separate GPU pools.
Difficulty classifier assigning levels 1-5, used for routing, length-penalty budgets, and batching.

Continued pretraining on seed competitive-programming corpora (TACO, LeetCode, USACO, CodeContests, IOI, crawled) expanded with Gemini 3.1 Pro and reasoning traces from Claude 4.6 / Gemini 3.1; 20% of examples converted to hypothesis-conditioned form.

SFT on non-synthetic problems with reference solutions via solution matching across six frontier LLMs, plus for hard problems selecting reasoning traces by a two-term likelihood score (forward trace/solution likelihood + reverse question likelihood under the base model).
Progressive 3-stage summarizer training (local-step RL on information-preservation score, end-to-end chain RL, then joint RL with main solver).

Multi-component RL: reward = executability gate, correctness vs gold/brute-force, then speedup-over-brute-force efficiency; hypothesis reward combines verification pass rate with downstream gain S(x,h) - S(x, empty); difficulty-dependent thinking-length penalty.
LoRA-only updates to pi_main per problem instance; auxiliary policies frozen.
Rank-based smoothed best-of-N objective with exponential rank weights w_j proportional to exp(-lambda j), lambda annealed upward from average-reward to max-reward optimization.

Context includes prior candidate solutions with scores plus an online-updated global summary of explored strategies; direct high-parallel generation used for easy problems, test-time RL reserved for hard ones.
Asynchronous pipeline-RL with token-level staleness weighting (exponential decay past K1, drop past K2) combined with Agentic GRPO.
Pipelined context parallelism for the DeltaNet+softmax hybrid, plus dynamic CP size by difficulty, difficulty/length-balanced batching across DP workers, and frozen MoE router during RL.

Three live Codeforces rounds (1087, 1088, 1089; Mar 2026) with two scoring conventions: S(separate) per-solution-at-ready-time and S(joint) single-account submissions delayed to avoid AI-detection scrutiny.

100-problem internal benchmark evenly split over 5 difficulty levels, metrics: accept rate, Level-5 solved out of 20, difficulty-weighted score; baselines Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen 3.5-397B.
200-problem set for hypothesis-generation pass@1/pass@5; 50 real Codeforces problems judged by the official hidden tests for test-case generation.

key_findings.finding: GrandCode placed first in three consecutive live Codeforces contests, beating all human participants including legendary grandmasters.
key_findings.evidence: Rounds 1087, 1088, 1089 (Mar 21/28/29, 2026): S(separate) scores 9269, 16511, 11596 and S(joint) 8334, 15008, 9506, with all tasks finished first in each round (finish times 00:51:11, 01:40:35, 00:56:43), documented by standings/submission screenshots.

key_findings.finding: Each training stage contributes cumulative gains on the internal benchmark, with RL and test-time RL driving the largest improvements on the hardest problems.
key_findings.evidence: On 100 problems: base Qwen 3.5-397B 64% accept / 4-of-20 Level 5 / 52.2 weighted; +continued training 71% / 6 / 61.0; +SFT 73% / 7 / 62.5; +full RL 81% / 13 / 72.3; +test-time RL 85% / 15 / 73.5, versus 75% / 7 / 64.3 for the best frontier baseline (Gemini 3.1 Pro).

key_findings.finding: Difference-driven test generation plus solution attack makes the self-constructed test suite nearly as discriminative as Codeforces' hidden tests.
key_findings.evidence: On 50 real Codeforces problems judged by the official system, solutions passing the base suite were accepted 42/50; after difference-driven generation and solution attack 48/50; adding submission feedback with continued online generation reached 50/50.

key_findings.finding: Training the hypothesis-proposal module substantially improves verified-conjecture quality.
key_findings.evidence: On a 200-problem set, pass@1/pass@5 rose from 34%/44% (Qwen-3.5-27B) to 45%/52% with SFT and 52%/57% with SFT+RL.

key_findings.finding: Pipelined context parallelism recovers most of the utilization lost to DeltaNet's sequential recurrence.
key_findings.evidence: For the 3-DeltaNet+softmax block, DeltaNet/overall efficiency goes 67%/87% at 2 micro-batches, 80%/90.3% at 4, 89%/94% at 8, 94%/97% at 16, approaching N/(N+3) -> 100%.
